messages.subject: Simplex
parts:
Hi everybody, I have a simple question:

It's correct assign to each value of a simplex something like this?


parameters{
simplex[C] theta[N];
} 
transformed parameters{
 for (i in 1:N){
  theta[i,1] = d[i]*exp(g[i]+b[i]*Z[i]);  // Z is a real number >=0
  theta[i,2] = d[i]*exp(g[i]+b[i]*Z[i]);
  theta[i,3] = d[i]*exp(g[i]+b[i]*Z[i]);
 }
}
model{
  d~gamma(4,2);
  g~improper uniform;
  b~improper uniform;
  
 ....~dirichlet(theta[i]);

}

or what is the best way to do this ??

thank you in advance

David

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Simplex
parts:
On Friday, March 24, 2017 at 11:12:32 PM UTC-4, David Vivas wrote:
Hi everybody, I have a simple question:

It's correct assign to each value of a simplex something like this?

No. If theta is declared in the parameters block of a Stan program, then it is already a simplex and you cannot assign anything to its elements.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simplex
parts:
And if you declare it as a transformed parameter and
assign in that block, you'll need to actually assign it
to a simplex (non-negative values summing to one). Also,
your example assigns exactly the same value to each member
of the simplex, which is probably not what you intended.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Simplex
parts: On Sunday, March 26, 2017 at 6:07:24 PM UTC-4, David Vivas wrote:

Oh I'm sorry ! 
I really wanted mean something like this:

transformed parameters{
    simplex[C] theta[N];
      for (i in 1:N){
         theta[i,1] = d[i] * exp(g1[i]+b1[i]*Z[i]);  // Z is a real number >=0
         theta[i,2] = d[i] * exp(g2[i]+b2[i]*Z[i]);
         theta[i,3] = d[i] * exp(g3[i]+b3[i]*Z[i]);
      }
}

Please Ben, my question is : If I want to use a vector as parameter of a dirichlet distribution (summing to one) but the components of this vector are for example (3,9,12),  I suppose I should turn my vector  into something like this: (3/S, 9/S, 12/S) where S=3+9+12, or there's a best way to do it ??   (I assumed that the simplex did that work)

That construction has the property that you can multiply each element of z by a positive constant and get the same simplex, in which case the posterior scale of z is only affected by the prior. Unless there is a good reason not to, the best way to do it is to declare

simplex[C] theta[N];

in the parameters block and not worry about constructing it in the transformed parameters block.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simplex
parts:
> On Mar 26, 2017, at 6:14 PM, David Vivas <vivad...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
...
>
> ... If I want to use a vector as parameter of a dirichlet distribution (summing to one) but the components of this vector are for example (3,9,12), I suppose I should turn my vector into something like this: (3/S, 9/S, 12/S) where S=3+9+12, to ensure that their componentes sum 1, or there's a best way to do it ?? (I assumed that the simplex did that work)

When you have Dirichlet(y | alpha), the outcome y must be a K-simplex and
the parameter alpha must be a positive K-vector. So [3, 9, 12] (as a column
vector) is a perfectly reasonable value for alpha.

- Bob
